# Case study: the output of a four-step model {#sec-m1-modelo4etapas}

::: {.modulo-meta}
**Data:** `dados/processados/modelo4etapas/links_rmc_2018_completo.parquet`
**Source:** PTV VISUM export, morning peak hour, Curitiba Metropolitan Region (RMC; 2018
network, 2017 counts)
**Common thread:** this same dataset comes back in modules 2 to 5
:::

The previous chapters worked with a public dataset that was already tabulated. This one works with the
other kind of file that lands on a transport planner's desk: the **export of a
simulation model**. R here is not the modelling tool, it is the
post-processing tool, which is how most technical teams actually use the language.

The question is that of any technical note:

> *How much does the network carry, how much does it lose to congestion, and where are the bottlenecks?*

It looks like a sum. We will see that it is not.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)

ggplot2::theme_set(
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    ggplot2::theme(panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank(),
                   plot.title = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold"),
                   legend.position = "bottom")
)
```
:::


## Step 1: Read the file

The extract is in Parquet, a columnar format that takes a fraction of the original shapefile's space and is
read in a fraction of the time (SQL with DuckDB, @sec-m3-duckdb). Reading it directly through DuckDB, without loading anything
that is not needed:


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
con <- duckdb::dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb())

links <- DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "
  SELECT *
  FROM 'dados/processados/modelo4etapas/links_rmc_2018_completo.parquet'
")

duckdb::dbDisconnect(con, shutdown = TRUE)

dim(links)
#> [1] 208336     36
```
:::



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
links |>
  dplyr::select(no, name, sentido, typeno, numlanes, capprt, v0prt, volvehprt, vc) |>
  dplyr::slice_head(n = 5) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

::: {.cell-output-display}


| no|name                       |sentido | typeno| numlanes| capprt| v0prt| volvehprt|   vc|
|--:|:--------------------------|:-------|------:|--------:|------:|-----:|---------:|----:|
|  2|Rodoanel Contorno Leste    |direto  |     11|        2|   3000|   110|      2179| 0.73|
|  2|Rodoanel Contorno Leste    |inverso |     11|        2|   3000|   110|         0| 0.00|
|  8|Rua General Mário Tourinho |direto  |     32|        3|   3900|    50|         0| 0.00|
|  8|Rua General Mário Tourinho |inverso |     32|        3|   3900|    50|      1557| 0.40|
|  9|Rua General Mário Tourinho |direto  |     32|        3|   3900|    50|      1481| 0.38|


:::
:::


Before getting into the numbers, it is worth seeing what we are talking about: the same table also exists
as a spatial layer (`dados/processados/modelo4etapas/rede_rmc_2018.gpkg`), with one row
per road segment. A static map, coloured by the volume/capacity ratio (`vc`), already
shows the shape of the network and where it is most loaded:


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
rede <- sf::st_read("dados/processados/modelo4etapas/rede_rmc_2018.gpkg", quiet = TRUE)

ggplot2::ggplot(rede) +
  ggplot2::geom_sf(ggplot2::aes(colour = vc), linewidth = 0.25) +
  ggplot2::scale_colour_viridis_c(option = "rocket", direction = -1, name = "vc") +
  ggplot2::theme_void(base_size = 10)
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![Model road network, coloured by the volume/capacity ratio (vc)](m1-08b-modelo4etapas_files/figure-html/fig-rede-preview-1.png){#fig-rede-preview width=1200}
:::
:::


We come back to this spatial layer more calmly in @sec-m2 (reprojection, length, static
maps); here it only serves to let you see the network before diving into the table.

## Step 2: Three questions before any calculation

**1. What is the unit of observation?** The temptation is to say "one link". That is wrong:


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
c(
  linhas        = nrow(links),
  links_unicos  = dplyr::n_distinct(links$no),
  link_sentido  = nrow(dplyr::distinct(links, no, sentido))
)
#>       linhas links_unicos link_sentido 
#>       208336       104168       208336
```
:::


Each physical link appears **twice**, once per direction (`sentido`). The key is `no` + `sentido`.
Grouping by `no` without noticing this mixes the two directions of each road.

::: {.callout-warning}
## The same network, two conventions

The original export brings the same network in **two different formats**: one file with one
row per direction (the one we are using) and another with both directions on the **same row**, in
columns prefixed with `R_`. It is the classic case of long versus wide format
(@sec-m1-manipulacao). Adding the two exports together counts everything twice.
:::

**2. Do the data cover what is expected?**


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
links |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    tipos_de_via   = dplyr::n_distinct(typeno),
    extensao_km    = round(sum(comprimento_km, na.rm = TRUE)),
    com_volume     = sum(volvehprt > 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    com_contagem   = sum(tem_contagem, na.rm = TRUE),
    postos         = dplyr::n_distinct(id_posto[tem_contagem])
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

::: {.cell-output-display}


| tipos_de_via| extensao_km| com_volume| com_contagem| postos|
|------------:|-----------:|----------:|------------:|------:|
|           37|       28257|      79680|           63|     26|


:::
:::


Twenty-five counting stations for a 28,000-kilometre network. It is not much, and it is what
exists. Knowing this before promising a validation is part of the job.

**3. Are there impossible values or sentinels?**


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
c(
  sem_acesso      = sum(links$sem_acesso, na.rm = TRUE),
  tsys_vazio      = sum(is.na(links$tsysset) | links$tsysset == ""),
  capacidade_zero = sum(links$capprt == 0, na.rm = TRUE)
)
#>      sem_acesso      tsys_vazio capacidade_zero 
#>           23290           13693            2871
```
:::


The 23,290 links flagged as `sem_acesso` (no access) had, in the original file, a travel time
of **360,000,000**. It is not a time: it is the sentinel VISUM uses to say "this
transport system cannot use this link". Whoever computes an average time without handling this
value gets a meaningless number, and R does not complain.

## Step 3: The units trap

This is the part that justifies the chapter. VISUM exports fields whose **name does not match
the unit stored**. Look at the first link of the Contorno Leste (the eastern ring road):


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
links |>
  dplyr::filter(no == 2, sentido == "direto") |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    name,
    volume          = volvehprt,
    comprimento_km,
    campo_VEHKMTRAVPRT = vehkmtravprt,
    conferencia     = volvehprt * comprimento_km
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

::: {.cell-output-display}


|name                    | volume| comprimento_km| campo_VEHKMTRAVPRT| conferencia|
|:-----------------------|------:|--------------:|------------------:|-----------:|
|Rodoanel Contorno Leste |   2179|          0.135|           294289.8|     294.243|


:::
:::


The field is called `VEHKMTRAVPRT`, "vehicle-kilometres travelled". It should be
2,179 × 0.135 = **294**. It is **294,290**. It is in **metres**, not kilometres.

The same goes for time: `VEHHOURTRAVTCUR`, "vehicle-hours", is in **seconds**. And
`VOLCAPRATIOPRT` is a **percentage**, not a ratio.

The extract already has the corrected columns (`veic_km`, `veic_h_livre`, `veic_h_carreg`, `vc`:
vehicle-km, vehicle-hours in free flow and loaded, and the v/c ratio),
but the habit that matters is checking: **recompute the indicator by an independent
route and see whether it matches.**


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
links |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    soma_do_campo = sum(veic_km, na.rm = TRUE),
    recalculado   = sum(volvehprt * comprimento_km, na.rm = TRUE),
    diferenca_pct = round(100 * (recalculado / soma_do_campo - 1), 3)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

::: {.cell-output-display}


| soma_do_campo| recalculado| diferenca_pct|
|-------------:|-----------:|-------------:|
|     3,676,335|   3,589,250|        -2.369|


:::
:::


::: {.callout-important}
## The error that throws no error

If you add up `VEHKMTRAVPRT` trusting its name, you get 3.7 **billion** vehicle-kilometres
in a metropolitan region of 3 million inhabitants. The code runs, the chart looks nice, and
the number is a thousand times wrong. No warning message appears. The only defence is
checking by an independent route.
:::

## Step 4: The network totals


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
totais <- links |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    veic_km         = sum(veic_km, na.rm = TRUE),
    veic_h_livre    = sum(veic_h_livre, na.rm = TRUE),
    veic_h_carreg   = sum(veic_h_carreg, na.rm = TRUE),
    atraso_veic_h   = sum(atraso_veic_h, na.rm = TRUE),
    vel_media_kmh   = sum(veic_km, na.rm = TRUE) / sum(veic_h_carreg, na.rm = TRUE),
    vel_livre_kmh   = sum(veic_km, na.rm = TRUE) / sum(veic_h_livre, na.rm = TRUE),
    links_saturados = sum(vc >= 1, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

totais |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(dplyr::everything(), ~ round(.x, 1))) |>
  knitr::kable(format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

::: {.cell-output-display}


|   veic_km| veic_h_livre| veic_h_carreg| atraso_veic_h| vel_media_kmh| vel_livre_kmh| links_saturados|
|---------:|------------:|-------------:|-------------:|-------------:|-------------:|---------------:|
| 3,676,335|       67,755|       176,158|       108,403|          20.9|          54.3|           3,436|


:::
:::


Keep these numbers: **3,676,335 vehicle-kilometres** and **108,403 vehicle-hours of delay**
(`atraso`) in the peak hour. After any filter or `join`, check against them. It is the same principle
as in @sec-m1-joins: the known total is your anchor.

## Step 5: Where the delay is (and why the total is misleading)

Now the question the technical note really asks. Let us classify the roads by the tens digit of the
model's type code (motorway and expressway, arterial, collector, local, local access and
connector, no loading):


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
classes <- links |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    classe = dplyr::case_when(
      typeno %/% 10 == 1            ~ "1. Rodovia e via expressa",
      typeno %/% 10 %in% c(2, 3)    ~ "2. Arterial",
      typeno %/% 10 == 4            ~ "3. Coletora",
      typeno %/% 10 %in% c(5, 6)    ~ "4. Local",
      typeno %/% 10 == 7            ~ "5. Acesso local e conector",
      .default                      = "6. Sem carregamento"
    )
  ) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    links       = dplyr::n(),
    extensao_km = sum(comprimento_km, na.rm = TRUE),
    veic_km     = sum(veic_km, na.rm = TRUE),
    atraso_h    = sum(atraso_veic_h, na.rm = TRUE),
    .by = classe
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    pct_veic_km = 100 * veic_km / sum(veic_km),
    pct_atraso  = 100 * atraso_h / sum(atraso_h)
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(classe)

classes |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

::: {.cell-output-display}


|classe                     |   links| extensao_km|   veic_km| atraso_h| pct_veic_km| pct_atraso|
|:--------------------------|-------:|-----------:|---------:|--------:|-----------:|----------:|
|1. Rodovia e via expressa  |   3,647|     1,205.6| 803,734.4|  2,611.7|        21.9|        2.4|
|2. Arterial                |  11,628|     1,376.5| 983,410.5|  6,995.4|        26.7|        6.5|
|3. Coletora                |  17,873|     1,706.0| 674,440.7|  6,035.3|        18.3|        5.6|
|4. Local                   |  35,446|     9,788.8| 819,989.1| 10,500.4|        22.3|        9.7|
|5. Acesso local e conector | 136,881|    13,605.6| 394,760.4| 82,260.2|        10.7|       75.9|
|6. Sem carregamento        |   2,861|       574.9|       0.0|      0.0|         0.0|        0.0|


:::
:::


The result is uncomfortable and it is the point of the chapter: the **"local access and
connector"** category accounts for about 11% of vehicle-kilometres and for **76% of all the network's
delay**. These are access links with volume/capacity ratios of 7, 8, 11.

This is not real congestion. It is a **modelling artefact**: the connector is the seam through
which a zone's demand enters the network, and it does not represent a road with physical capacity.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
links |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(atraso_veic_h)) |>
  dplyr::slice_max(atraso_veic_h, n = 8) |>
  dplyr::transmute(no, name, typeno, volvehprt, vc = round(vc, 1),
                   atraso_h = round(atraso_veic_h)) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

::: {.cell-output-display}


|     no|name                                 | typeno| volvehprt|   vc| atraso_h|
|------:|:------------------------------------|------:|---------:|----:|--------:|
| 124919|NA                                   |     71|      2231| 11.2|    23089|
|  20424|Rua Edgard Moutinho Zandoná          |     70|      3387|  8.5|    15747|
|  65913|Rua Maria de Lourdes Grabowski Kampa |     70|      2892|  7.2|     7458|
| 130806|NA                                   |     71|      1233|  6.2|     3565|
| 122592|NA                                   |     71|      1513|  7.6|     3117|
| 122593|NA                                   |     71|      1513|  7.6|     2184|
|   6202|Rua Alfredo Pinto                    |     50|      2973|  3.7|     1169|
|  17477|Rua Aquelino Orestes Baglioli        |     60|      3040|  3.8|     1165|


:::
:::


Notice that the worst cases have no road name. They are exactly the connectors.

::: {.callout-important}
## The indicator you publish changes with what you include

Reporting "108 thousand hours of delay in the peak hour" without qualification is reporting, three quarters of it,
a model artefact. Restricting to the real network (motorways, arterials and collectors), the delay
drops to about **15.6 thousand vehicle-hours**.

Both calculations are "right" in the sense that the code ran. Only one of them can be
defended in a meeting.
:::


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
classes |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(pct_veic_km, pct_atraso),
                      names_to = "indicador", values_to = "pct") |>
  dplyr::mutate(indicador = dplyr::recode(indicador,
                                          pct_veic_km = "Vehicle-km",
                                          pct_atraso  = "Delay")) |>
  ggplot2::ggplot(ggplot2::aes(x = pct, y = forcats::fct_rev(classe), fill = indicador)) +
  ggplot2::geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::label_percent(scale = 1)) +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = c("Vehicle-km" = "#1a5b8a", "Delay" = "#c2542d")) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = NULL,
                title = "Where the network carries traffic and where it loses time",
                subtitle = "Curitiba region, morning peak hour, 2018 model")
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![Share of each road class in vehicle-kilometres and in total delay.](m1-08b-modelo4etapas_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-12-1.png){width=1200}
:::
:::


## Step 6: The defensible subset


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
rede_real <- links |> dplyr::filter(typeno < 50)

rede_real |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    links         = dplyr::n(),
    extensao_km   = round(sum(comprimento_km, na.rm = TRUE)),
    veic_km       = round(sum(veic_km, na.rm = TRUE)),
    atraso_veic_h = round(sum(atraso_veic_h, na.rm = TRUE)),
    vel_media_kmh = round(sum(veic_km, na.rm = TRUE) / sum(veic_h_carreg, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
    saturados     = sum(vc >= 1, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

::: {.cell-output-display}


|  links| extensao_km|   veic_km| atraso_veic_h| vel_media_kmh| saturados|
|------:|-----------:|---------:|-------------:|-------------:|---------:|
| 33,174|       4,290| 2,461,586|        15,642|          45.8|     1,837|


:::
:::


Average speed of 45.8 km/h on the structural network, against 20.9 km/h for the total. The whole
difference comes from deciding, deliberately, what goes into the calculation. **That decision is the analysis.**

## Checking checklist

This is the habit the course wants to build, and it comes back in every module:

::: {.callout-tip}
## Before publishing any number that comes out of a model

1. **Unit of observation.** How many rows per physical object? Count `distinct` on the key
   you believe is unique.
2. **Units of measurement.** Recompute at least one indicator by an independent route and
   compare. Never trust the field name.
3. **Sentinels.** Look for absurd values (`360000000`, `-1`, `9999`) before computing
   averages.
4. **Anchor totals.** Record the totals of the full dataset and check against them after
   each filter and each `join`.
5. **What goes into the calculation.** Separate the real network from modelling artefacts, and state that
   choice in the report.
:::

## What comes next

This same dataset runs through the rest of the course:

| Module | What we will do with it |
|:--|:--|
| @sec-m2 | Read the spatial layer, reproject, check the computed length against the stored one, map loading and saturation |
| @sec-m3 | Compare the model with the 25 field counts, treat the network as a graph |
| Module 4 | Combine the stops and BRT corridors with accessibility |
| Module 5 | Produce a parameterised report, one per municipality in the region |

::: {.callout-note}
## About the source of the data

The extract used here was processed from a PTV VISUM export shared for teaching
purposes. The script that produces the extract from the original files is in
`scripts/00-gera-recorte-modelo4etapas.R`, and the field dictionary in
`dados/processados/modelo4etapas/`. See [Example data](a-dados.qmd).
:::
